surfaces.part: lit foliage canopy mass (top of bush)

answer.evidence: The silhouette widens from 2 px at row 7 to 27 px at rows 15-16, then narrows to 18 px at row 25 and 7 px at row 26. Rows 7-16 are a lit canopy: the column scan goes from a light highlight (L=159, #94b353) at rows 7-10 down to mid greens (L=78-103). A dark line at row 17 (x=16 L=22, x=23 L=36) marks the front edge, and rows 18-19 read as shadow below it. Rows 17-26 are a darker shaded underside (L=22-55) that works as the front face, about 10 rows. There is no side face. The organic mound shows a lit top and a dark front, so it reads as 3/4 view rather than a flat elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small dark-green bush, much smaller than the references and drawn with only 6 distinct colours in total. The per-tile measurements are 0 because the piece is under one tile, so I judged by eye. It shows about 3-4 green steps: a lighter top highlight, a mid green and a dark underside. Clump structure is only hinted at, with a few scalloped edge bumps and no distinct leaf clusters or per-clump highlights. The outline is not a black line, since the dark edge pixels are tinted green (0% neutral), but it is hardly separate from the dark shadow tone, so I call it mixed. Reference tree-1a786c has 7 visible tones per tile and tree-d43edd has 29, each with layered leaf clumps and highlights. The candidate looks flatter and thinner next to them, closer to a sticker blob than a Beodeul canopy. It is also described as 2x2 tiles but looks well under that size. A careful artist would not accept it beside the references without more clump and shade steps.

Rows 7-16 show a light-green sunlit crown (L~159 at the top of columns 8 and 16) that steps down into mid greens (L~78-103). Rows 17-25 are darker, shaded foliage (L~22-55) forming the front/underside, with the darkest rows at the bottom. The top is lit and the front is shadowed, so it reads as a volume seen from above at 3/4. It is not a flat slab and not a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is about 30x21 source px, so the per-tile facts read 0 and I judged it by eye. It has only 6 distinct colours in total, which is a thin ramp next to the references: 1a786c has 7 visible tones per tile and d43edd has 29. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans green and counts as dark_material_tone, like the references. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills, but the bush reads as a dark mass with a few lighter leaf dabs on top. It has less clump separation, less highlight variety and less internal leaf detail than either reference, and its overall contrast is low. Both references show layered leaf clusters in several greens, with light tops, shadowed undersides and clear edge breakup. The candidate looks flatter and closer to a simple blob, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar. When in doubt, fail.
